severity_examples.condition: Task 19/20 run to completion (package.json renamed, marketplace row updated, settings keys swapped) before anyone confirms who currently owns the `linsenkasten-mcp` name on npm.

severity_examples.condition: Some repo outside the 8 named files (or outside interlock/lattice/core-interweave) has a settings.json/settings.local.json entry referencing `mcp__interlens__*` by name, and that repo is never swept.
severity_examples.scenario: A permission-allowlist entry in some other repo's settings.json (e.g. a `Bash`/tool rule naming `mcp__interlens__search_lenses` literally) stops matching the moment the MCP server key becomes `mcp__linsenkasten__*`, silently degrading to a permission prompt or denial with no error pointing at the rename as the cause — Task 20 step 5's file list names 8 specific Clavain files and a 'grep interlock/lattice/core-interweave, edit only live config' instruction, but nothing instructs grepping other repos' settings files for the tool-name prefix itself.

severity_examples.condition: Task 20 executes while `feat/linsenkasten` is still an unmerged branch relative to whatever `main` currently is at that point.
severity_examples.scenario: The plan never states whether `feat/linsenkasten`'s work (all of Stages A-D) merges into `main` before Task 20 step 1 renames the GitHub repo and step 2 moves the directory / repoints the remote — if the worktree branch is still unmerged when this runs, the directory everyone works from after the rename may not actually contain the local-engine/harvest work the rest of the plan built.
